children: Tyson Foods said its revenue will grow by less than previously expected this year, citing pressure on volatile cattle prices.
The company said Thursday that it expects revenue in fiscal 2026 to rise by 1.5% to 2%, down from a previous range of 2.5% to 3.5%.
Shares fell 6.8% to $52.00 in pre-market trading.

"The revised outlook is primarily driven by significant margin compression amid volatile cattle prices and one of the most severe cattle shortages in U.S. history, as well as the expected impact of lower cattle prices on the value of live cattle inventories," the company said Thursday.

The beef segment is now expected to generate an adjusted operating loss of $625 million to $775 million for the fiscal year, compared with Tyson's previous guidance for a loss between $500 million and $650 million.
Tyson also cut guidance for adjusted operating profits for its other meat segments.

The company in August said it was restructuring its beef network around three facilities in the central U.S. to address the cattle shortage. Those actions should reduce operating cost pressures in fiscal 2027, Chief Executive Officer Donnie King said.
